properties.title: NRC Report: Ammonia, Anhydrous near Baton Rouge, LA
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 914704 - Medium Affected: AIR - Suspected Responsible Party: LION COPOLYMER, LLC
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 914704
Incident Time: 2009-08-06 23:30:00
Nearest City: Baton Rouge, LA
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: AMMONIA, ANHYDROUS
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: LION COPOLYMER, LLC
Skytruth Analysis
– A POWER OUTAGE OCCURRED AT APPROXIMATELY 6:30 PM ON AUGUST 6TH DUE TO A BIRD NEST FOUND ON A SWITCH IN OUR “D” SUBSTATION. THE NEST WAS FOUND TO HAVE SEVERAL METAL WIRES INCORPORATED THROUGHOUT. THIS SUBSEQUENTLY SHUTDOWN OUR 15 KV FEEDER WHICH POWERED OUR AMMONIA COMPRESSOR SYSTEM. WITH THE AMMONIA COMPRESSOR SYSTEM DOWN, THE PRESSURE STARTED TO INCREASE AS THE SYSTEM INCREASED IN TEMPERATURE. AFTER A PERIOD OF TIME, THE PRESSURE BUILT UP IN OUR PRIMARY AMMONIA STORAGE TANK, CAUSING THE PRESSURE RELIEF DEVICE ON THE TANK TO LIFT, SENDING AMMONIA TO THE FLARE. IN ANTICIPATION OF THE RELEASE, THE NATURAL GAS FLOW WAS INCREASED TO THE FLARE HEADER TO ASSIST IN THE AMMONIA COMBUSTION. ONCE THE POWER WAS RESTORED TO THAT CIRCUIT AROUND 2:30 AM ON AUGUST 7, THE AMMONIA COMPRESSOR WAS RESTARTED AND THE PRESSURE IMMEDIATELY CAME BACK INTO CONTROL. BASED ON CALCULATIONS AND FLARE DESTRUCTION EFFICIENCY FOR AMMONIA, APPROXIMATELY 1308.5 LBS. OF AMMONIA WAS RELEASED UNCOMBUSTED THROUGH THE FLARE OVER THE DURATION OF THE EVENT. FOR THE PURPOSES OF CALCULATING THE QUANTITY OF RELEASE, IT WAS CONSERVATIVELY ASSUMED THAT THE AMMONIA VENTED TO THE FLARE FOR THE DURATION OF THE POWER OUTAGE; HOWEVER, IT TOOK TIME AFTER THE INITIAL POWER OUTAGE FOR PRESSURE TO BUILD TO THE POINT THAT THE RELIEF DEVICE VENTED. OFFSITE ODORS WERE REPORTED TO US FROM SURROUNDING FACILITIES. FACILITY PERSONNEL DROVE THE SURROUNDING ROADS TO THE SOUTH, EAST, AND NORTH OF THE FACILITY BETWEEN 10:00 PM AND 10:30 PM AND NO ODORS WERE DETECTED. LOUISIANA STATE POLICE AND LOUISIANA DEPT. OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY WERE NOTIFIED PROMPTLY DURING THE INCIDENT AT 9:38 PM ON 8/6/09. FOLLOW UP REPORT WAS MADE TO LSP ON 8/7/09 AND WRITTEN FOLLOWUP WAS SENT TO LSP, LDEQ, AND THE LEPC ON 8/11/09.

THE TRACTOR TRAILER STRUCK THE FORD RANGER, CAUSING THE DRIVER SIDE SADDLE TANK TO RUPTURE. THE SADDLE TANK RELEASED 90 TO 100 GALLONS OF DIESEL ONTO A BRIDGE ON I-20 WESTBOUND MILE MARKER 131. THE RELEASED DIESEL MADE ITS WAY INTO THE NEARBY STORM DRAINS, AND THE CALLER BELIEVES THAT THE DIESEL THEN MADE ITS WAY INTO VARIOUS UNNAMED CREEKS BELOW THE BRIDGE. THE CALLER STATED DURING THE COURSE OF THE ACCIDENT A GUARD RAIL WAS STRUCK AND SUSTAINED UNKNOWN DAMAGES. THE DRIVER OF THE FORD RANGER SUFFERED UNKNOWN INJURIES AND WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL BY THEIR SIGNIFICANT OTHER. I-20 WEST BOUND HAS BEEN CLOSED FOR 2 HOUR BECAUSE OF THIS ACCIDENT AND REMAINS CLOSED

properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 938937 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: U.S.A. TRUCK INC.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 938937
Incident Time: 2010-05-03 09:50:00
Nearest City: Norwich, CT
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: OIL: DIESEL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: U.S.A. TRUCK INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 60 gallons
A TRACTOR-TRAILER VEHICLE MAKING A DELIVERY TO THE FACILITY ACCIDENTALLY STRUCK A GUARD RAIL WHILE TURNING IN THE PARKING LOT AND RUPTURED A FUEL TANK RELEASING AN ESTIMATED 60 GALLONS OF FUEL OIL TO THE PAVEMENT. IT WAS RAINING HEAVILY AT THE TIME AND THE FUEL OIL WAS CARRIED BY STORM WATER TO A NEARBY STORM DRAIN, FLOWED THROUGH SEVERAL CATCH BASINS, AND ULTIMATELY DISCHARGED FROM THE STORM WATER OUTFALL TO THE YANTIC RIVER. A LIGHT SHEEN WAS OBSERVED ON THE RIVER FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT. ABSORBANT PADS/SOCKS WERE PLACED ADJACENT TO THE SPILL AREA AND WITHIN THE CATCH BASINS IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE SPILL, AND A SPILL RESPONSE COMPANY WAS BROUGHT TO THE FACILITY FOR FINAL CLEAN UP.
